speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry of the 1,000 companies that qualify under Condition 1 of the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities scheme, what is the breakdown of the number between foreign companies and local enterprises.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My question was really, of the 1,000 or so who are qualified, how many are locally owned businesses as opposed to foreign MNCs?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I have another supplementary question, which is relating to the press release that was put up by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The press release said that "at the end of the two-year period, firms would have to demonstrate that they maintained their local workforce share during this period".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, the M-SEP scheme is actually allowing firms to hire more work pass and S Pass holders during the two-year period.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I just wanted to clarify, what that sentence is referring to: at the end of the two-year period, firms would also have to maintain their local workforce share.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Because, if you are allowed to hire more of these work pass and S Pass holders, by definition, would your local workforce share not go down at the end of that two-year period?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Unless you are not exercising as a company, the ability to hire more of those, which would also defeat the point of the scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member’s first supplementary question, the actual proportion depends on the firms which successfully apply for the initiatives listed, which is under Condition 1.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For me to go through the exact details of the M-SEP scheme itself, perhaps the Member could separately file a Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, these firms must be locally incorporated or registered.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In this particular way, M-SEP is very selective in targeting firms or investments which will grow our economy and our competitiveness.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And to be part of these programmes, the firms would have been working closely with our economic agencies like Economic Development Board (EDB) or Enterprise Singapore (ESG).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's second point in terms of the end of the two-year period, it should not be taken in isolation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If you look at the overall flow in terms of the scheme from the fulfilment of Condition 1, then the two-year mark in terms of a higher concentration of foreign workforce or that potential should not be any impediment whatsoever.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because the ultimate fulfilment of the conditions is really about growing our economy, our competitiveness and at the same time, making sure that our locals continue to be put up front in terms of training and in terms of upskilling.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just a very quick one on the second supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: In terms of this reference “at the end of the two-year period where you have to maintain your local workforce share”, if I understand the Minister correctly, I suppose that is referring to just maintain the absolute number of locals that the firm is hiring, rather than the share of locals as a percentage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The entire focus as I have spent over an hour yesterday in my Committee of Supply (COS) speech doing, is to focus on levelling up our competitiveness, maintaining our lead against the whole business world.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Therefore, it is important that in the scheme that we put up – and today given where we are, we have actually very tightly scoped these companies that qualify under the M-SEP scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, you should look at it from that context.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the broader macroeconomics of how we look at our workforce, and the overall change, the one-third to two-third ratio will still maintain.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [	Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
